findings.title: Displacement Reverses Into Restoration
findings.claim: Across 17:103–104, Pharaoh intends to unsettle a people from the land, but he and his company are drowned; afterward the people targeted are told to settle on that land, and a later appointed gathering is brought by another agency.
findings.mechanism: The focus links intention to forced displacement from the earth and then to drowning of Pharaoh with everyone alongside him. The immediate sequel repeats the land, commands settlement, and names a promised future arrival of a mixed group. These contacts reverse who controls the ground and collective movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The drowning becomes part of a territorial reversal: the attempted removal gives way to the targeted people’s settlement, while the later mixed gathering remains distinct from Pharaoh’s drowned company.
findings.containment: The two ayat directly support attempted removal, drowning, subsequent settlement, and a later mixed gathering. They do not say that the drowned group and the later gathered group are identical or assign one moral status to every person in either group. The appointed-time, arrival, and mixed-gathering details are supplied branch images.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel support, focus morphology, and the exact 17:104 context occurrences ground the sequence; the territorial reversal is an interpretation of their ordered contact.
